english.title: Enter controlled building without permission / not in accordance with conditions / remain there when instructed to leave
english.standardoffencewording:

(A)_[entered a controlled building without the permission of]_
(B)_[entered a controlled building otherwise than in accordance with a condition, namely **(..SPECIFY CONDITION..), imposed with the permission of]_

english.legislation: Contrary to regulations 24 and 34 of the Port Security Regulations 2009.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
without lawful authority / reasonable excuse
entered a controlled building without the permission of a relevant person or not in accordance with condition imposed with the permission OR
remained in a controlled building after being instructed to leave by a relevant person
in breach of regulation 24 of the Port Security Regulations 2009

investigatoraction.description: Guilty Plea by letter procedure may be offered for this offence
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) As per regulation 34(2), a person is not guilty of this offence unless it is proved that, at the material time, notices stating that the building concerned was a controlled building were posted so as to be reasonably seen and read by a person entering the controlled building.
(ii) Regulation 36 creates a defence of due diligence in relation to this offence; in any proceedings against any person for an offence under the Regulations it is a defence for that person to show that they took all reasonable steps and exercised all due diligence to avoid committing the offence.

other.penalty:
Summary: Level 5 fine.

Note
On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates' court was removed - as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.

Time limit for prosecutions:
6 months
